article.name: Cashew
article.summary: Cashew is a local persistent thought graph for agent memory. Typed thought nodes and derivation edges are stored in SQLite; retrieval combines vector seeding with a bounded graph walk, while extraction and consolidation use model-assisted processing. This is a source-based review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

who_what.text: Cashew is a local thought-graph memory system for agents. Its repository describes SQLite storage, vector-seeded graph retrieval, LLM-backed extraction and autonomous think/sleep cycles. Retrieval uses local embeddings and does not require an API call.

architecture.text: The design specifies thought_nodes, derivation_edges and embeddings in SQLite, with sqlite-vec as an optional vector table. Nodes include content, type, domain, timestamps including optional referent time, source file, access counters, tags, metadata and decay/permanence state. Edges store parent/child relationships, weights and reasoning.

The design describes typed fact, observation, insight, decision, belief, derived, meta, core-memory and cross-link nodes. Multiple domains can coexist in one graph; domain filtering is applied at retrieval.

behavior.text: The README documents text extraction and ingestion for Obsidian, Markdown directories, OpenClaw session logs and Claude archives. It says LLM extraction is the default and offers a no-LLM paragraph-splitting mode. The design describes linking extracted nodes to similar parent nodes with derivation reasoning.

The documented maintenance model marks low-fitness nodes as decayed, excludes them from retrieval, and uses sleep cycles for cross-linking, near-duplicate consolidation, permanence promotion and decay. The audit module records decay transitions, writes a stub row if a node was already hard-deleted, truncates content summaries to 80 characters, and prunes old audit rows after seven days by default. The reviewed sources do not establish a general user-facing delete contract or content retention in backups and synchronized copies.

Retrieval embeds a query, searches for vector seed nodes, then expands through a bounded breadth-first graph walk and ranks returned context. The code supports optional domain and tag filters, filters decayed nodes, and can return node/path explanations. The README states that local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings are used and retrieval needs no API call.

The model offers domain labels and retrieval filters but the reviewed sources do not show tenant or principal access control. A local SQLite file is the documented deployment boundary; multi-user isolation was not verified.

Nodes can carry a source_file and edges can carry reasoning; decay audits preserve a snapshot at the transition. The reviewed contract does not require source URLs, evidence excerpts, author, trust state, citation validation or human approval, so this is partial lineage rather than a verified evidence chain.

metrics.evidence: Vector search and graph expansion are documented, but no answerability probes were run.
Sleep deduplication can merge near-duplicates; no correction sequence was scored.
Decay flags and filters are documented; no post-delete or residual-copy probes were run.
Domain filtering exists but no multi-principal isolation workload was run.
Source-file and derivation fields exist; no evidence-support adjudication was run.
The documented retrieval path was not timed.
Local embeddings and work caps are documented; no resource measurements were collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded read-only review of selected official source and documentation at the pinned head. Runtime behavior, every ingestion-to-database path, arbitrary hard-delete behavior, backup/sync retention, multi-user authorization, retrieval quality and operational performance were not established.

The documented vector seed scan is brute-force O(N), so cost grows with vector count; an ANN index is identified as a future need at substantially larger scale. The local embedding model requires a first-use download and local resources, and LLM-dependent extraction/think cycles require a configured provider.
No system operation, benchmark workload or tests were run. Project metrics and fixtures describe evaluation plans and are not Cashew results.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run. This review did not execute Cashew, its tests, or benchmark workloads.
